Reason for Mistake: The Planner at step 5 initiates an irreversible loop by misinterpreting the partial 3rd Earl page content as insufficient evidence, issuing redundant instructions to re-verify the 2nd Earl page. The Subtask Name: Initial Search and Lineage Correction
Step Range: 0-2
The Oracle: Identify the correct paternal grandfather by correcting the initial search error.
Evidence: Steps 0-2 involve the initial search returning an incorrect result (3rd Earl), the Planner analyzing the error, and the second search confirming the 2nd Earl as the father of the 3rd Earl.

The Subtask Name: Verification of Paternal Lineage via Wikipedia
Step Range: 3-10
The Oracle: Confirm the direct father-son chain (2nd Earl -> 3rd Earl -> 4th Earl) using Wikipedia pages.
Evidence: Steps 3-10 involve multiple WebSurfer calls to the 3rd Earl, 2nd Earl, and 4th Earl Wikipedia pages, repeatedly verifying that the 2nd Earl is the father of the 3rd Earl, who is the father of the 4th Earl.

The Subtask Name: Final Synthesis and Conclusion
Step Range: 11-21
The Oracle: Consolidate findings to definitively state the paternal grandfather's name and title.
Evidence: Steps 11-21 consist of repeated Planner analyses confirming the 2nd Earl as the grandfather and WebSurfer calls that do not yield new information, leading to the final conclusion based on the established lineage.

Loop detection rule: If steps show repeated reasoning patterns, retrying similar approaches, or cyclic agent/tool calls, mark them as loop-related. Otherwise set loop_role = none and loop_group_id = null.
